messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated artifact fetch errors from huggingface CDN (429/503) for model-fetcher service. Error-rate spike started 2026-03-15T08:18:00Z. Paging infra-oncall.

sarah: oncall responding. seeing 429/503s in fetcher logs, repeated GET failures to https://cdn-lfs.huggingface.co/models/*/pytorch_model.bin. stacktrace shows client-side retries timing out.

mike: confirmed. cold-start path failing on cache-miss -> network fetch. metrics: cold-start fail rate up to 30% last 10m, p95 latency from 450ms -> 2.3s for generation.

tanya: i can replicate with curl:
```
$ curl -I https://cdn-lfs.huggingface.co/models/abc/pytorch_model.bin
HTTP/2 429
x-request-id: rr18
retry-after: 3
```
-- also seeing intermittent 503s. status.huggingface.co shows no full outage but degraded.

elias: customer impact estimate? which customers/models affected?

sarah: initial signal: hosted API customers using models that fall back to HF-hosted artifacts on cache-miss. Customers with models already warmed in our S3 mirror unaffected. Potentially affects 18% of traffic for top-tier models during heavy churn windows.

mike: mitigation options: 1) flip artifact priority to our S3 mirror for the affected model ids 2) reduce parallel HF fetches client-side to avoid contributing to HF throttling 3) enable stronger exponential backoff and jitter to prevent retry storms 4) serve a smaller quantized fallback if the fetch fails.

tanya: i can push a canary env change to model-fetcher: `MODEL_ARTIFACT_PRIORITY=s3_cache,huggingface` (canary 1/10). will keep concurrency limits on the canary.

deploy-bot: sarah requested rollout: `kubectl -n inference set env deployment/model-fetcher MODEL_ARTIFACT_PRIORITY=s3_cache,huggingface` - starting canary (1/10).

mike: canary running. warming canary by prefetching artifacts from S3 mirror - downloads succeed, canary fetch latency ~70ms, error rate 0%.

tanya: reducing HF parallelism on all fetchers to 2: `export HF_MAX_PARALLEL=2` then rolling restart of fetcher pods. this reduces our fanout to huggingface during recovery window.

sarah: enabling client-side backoff too: `HF_RETRIES=3 HF_BACKOFF_BASE=0.5 HF_BACKOFF_JITTER=0.3`. pushing config now.

elias: good. can we also capture list of affected model ids for postmortem and customer comms? add to thread.

mike: capturing: [gpt-small-v2, llama-7b-legacy, rmt-finetune-2025] — those showed >5% fetch errors in the last 15m.

hf-support: (external) thanks for reporting. we're seeing elevated load on cdn-lfs shard serving those model artifacts. rate-limiting is in effect while we warm upstream caches. suggestion: use mirrored storage or enterprise CDN endpoints if available. ETA 20-45m for shard stabilization.

sarah: HF replied. we'll keep s3 priority set for 60m and re-evaluate. mike, leave canary at 10% for 15m then scale if stable. tanya, monitor error burn and open a pager if >10% error persists after 30m.

mike: acknowledged. I'll keep metrics dashboard pinned and post snapshots every 5m.

incident-bot: handoff reminder: current oncall tanya -> next oncall sarah at 08:23 UTC for 30m.

tanya: handing off to sarah. i'm staying on the channel until handoff completes; alerts muted for low-priority infra but open for fetcher errors.

sarah: picked up. i'll coordinate with support for a status page blurb: short notice that artifact fetch throttling from a third-party is increasing cold-start failures and latency for a subset of requests; mitigation in progress (mirrored artifacts + backoff). no customer-facing data loss.

mike: snapshot at 08:35 UTC: overall fetch error rate down from 30% -> 4% on prod (after canary + parallelism reduction). cold-start failures reduced accordingly.

elias: thanks. action items to record: 1) keep s3 mirror priority for 60m 2) maintain low HF parallelism + client backoff 3) collect list of affected model ids and sample request-ids for HF 4) open postmortem if incident lasts >60m 5) evaluate automated mirror promotion for high-traffic models to avoid single-CDN dependency.

tanya: noted and creating a short runbook update to fetcher docs: add `HF_MAX_PARALLEL` override, `MODEL_ARTIFACT_PRIORITY` runtime toggle, and emergency mirror promotion steps.

hf-support: (external) update: shard cache warming progressing, error-rate trending down. we will confirm when fully stable.

sarah: once HF confirms stable for 30m, we'll roll MODEL_ARTIFACT_PRIORITY back to its default and monitor. if we see flare-ups, we'll keep mirror preference until HF provides a durable fix or we implement more aggressive mirroring.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated (third-party rate-limiting). monitoring continues.

sarah: closing this thread for now — will file incident ticket and postmortem draft after we collect logs and HF confirmation. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
